# Principle

Anomalous or unexpected events and behaviours for systems (infrastructure, operating systems, applications and data) are analysed in a timely manner to detect cyber security events.

# Indicators of Good Practice

Not effective:
- No detection logic is deployed to identify unauthorised changes, anomalous authentication activity or suspicious software execution events originating from assets.
- Detection relies entirely on manual log review with no automated rules or alerting.

Partially effective:
- Detection logic exists but does not cover all three categories (unauthorised changes, anomalous authentication, suspicious execution).
- Rules are deployed but are not tested or tuned on a regular cycle defined by the organisation.

Fully effective:
- Detection logic is deployed, and unauthorised configuration changes, anomalous authentication patterns and suspicious process execution events are captured and produce alerts.
- Detection logic is tested and tuned on a regular cycle defined by the organisation to maintain effectiveness.
- Detection coverage is reviewed following cyber security incidents or significant environmental changes.
title: Ensure detection logic identifies unauthorised changes, anomalous authentication activity and suspicious software execution.
